title: Generation of recombinant vaccinia virus and analysis of virus-induced cell death
protocol: Seed BS-C-1 cells at 2.5 × 10^5 cells per well in 1 mL Complete MEM-10 medium on a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Culture the seeded cells for 16–20 hours in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Thaw vRB12 stock virus on ice.
Dilute virus to 0.5 × 10^5 pfu/mL using MEM-2.5 medium.
Aspirate the medium from the cell monolayer.
Replace it with 0.5 mL diluted virus.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 in an incubator for 2 hours.
Prewarm Opti-MEM and LT1 transfection reagent to 22°C.
Prepare a transfection master mix containing 100 μL Opti-MEM, 3 μL TransIT®-LT1 Transfection Reagent, and 1 μg pRB21-GFP-vIRD.
Incubate the DNA transfection mixture at 22°C for 15 minutes.
Retrieve virus-infected cells from step 1f.
Remove medium from virus-infected BS-C-1 cells.
Wash the infected cells twice by rinsing with 1 mL of 1X PBS.
Add 1 mL MEM-2.5 medium to the cells.
Add the DNA transfection mixture dropwise to the cells.
Gently rock the cells back and forth to mix the transfection mixture evenly.
Incubate the cells in a 37°C, 0.05% CO2 incubator for 24 hours.
Replace the medium with 1 mL MEM-2.5 medium.
Incubate the cells for 2 days in a 37°C, 0.05% CO2 incubator.
Prewarm Opti-MEM in a 37°C water bath.
Remove 500 μL of culture medium from each well.
Dislodge infected cells using a disposable cell scraper and transfer to a sterile screw-top microcentrifuge tube containing the remaining culture medium.
Place the tubes in dry ice for 5 minutes, followed by placing them in a 37°C water bath for 5 minutes.
Vortex the tubes for 5 seconds.
Repeat the freeze/thaw cycle two more times for a total of three cycles.
Centrifuge the viral supernatants at 650 × g and 22°C for 5 minutes to remove debris.
Store the purified viral supernatants at -80°C.
Seed BS-C-1 cells at 5 × 10^5 cells in 2 mL complete MEM-10 medium per well on a 6-well plate.
Incubate the seeded cells in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 24 hours.
Replace the medium with 1 mL of pre-warmed MEM-2.5 medium per well.
Thaw viral supernatants from step 3 on ice.
Dispense 100 μL, 10 μL, 1 μL or 0.1 μL of the thawed viral supernatant to each cell monolayer.
Incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 2 hours.
Remove the medium and replace it with 2 mL pre-warmed MEM-2.5 containing 2.5% methylcellulose.
Add the MEM-2.5% methylcellulose at an angle along the edge of the well to avoid air bubbles.
Incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 48 hours.
Dispense 0.5 mL of pre-warmed MEM-2.5 medium into sterile Eppendorf tubes.
Retrieve the plate from the incubator after 48–72 hours of infection.
Identify and mark large plaques at the bottom of the plate using a marker pen.
Scrape the plaque area carefully with a pipette tip while drawing up the content.
Transfer the scraped content to an Eppendorf tube containing 500 μL MEM-2.5.
Vortex the Eppendorf tube vigorously.
Subject the tube to three cycles of freeze/thaw in liquid nitrogen and a 37°C water bath.
Save the released virus at -80°C freezer until next round of selection.
Repeat steps 4–16 two more times for a total of three rounds of plaque selection.
Dispense the diluted virus to the BS-C-1 cells.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 minutes.
Add 1 mL of MEM-2.5 to each well.
Incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 48 hours.
Remove 1 mL of medium.
Scrape the cells in the remaining 1 mL of medium with a disposable cell scraper.
Transfer the cells and supernatant to a sterile Eppendorf tube.
Subject the infected cell mixture to three cycles of freeze/thaw.
Vortex the tube after each thaw cycle.
Save the viral supernatant in −80°C freezer.
Seed 1.5 × 10^6 of BS-C-1 cells in complete MEM medium in a T25 flask.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Dilute 500 μL of amplified recombinant virus with 1.5 mL MEM-2.5.
Dispense the diluted virus to the BS-C-1 cells in T25 flask.
Incubate virus with cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 minutes.
Add 3 mL of MEM-2.5 to the flask.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 48 hours.
Scrape the cells with a disposable cell scraper.
Transfer the supernatant to a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin the cells down at 1800 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL MEM-2.5.
Subject the cell mixture to three cycles of freeze/thaw.
Vortex the tube after each thaw cycle.
Save the viral supernatant in −80°C freezer.
Seed 2.5 × 10^5 L929 cells in 1 mL of complete DMEM-10 medium in each well of a 12-well plate.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Add 10 μL of the amplified recombinant virus to 1 mL MEM-2.5 and add this diluted virus to the cells.
Incubate the cells with the virus at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2 h.
Replace medium in each well with 1 mL of complete DMEM-10 medium.
Incubate infected cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 18 h.
Wash the infected cells by rinsing twice with 1 mL 1X PBS at 4°C.
Add 100 μL RIPA lysis buffer supplemented with 1X Complete protease inhibitor cocktail and 1X phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to each well.
Transfer cell lysate into an Eppendorf tube.
Homogenize the cell lysate by pressing it through an insulin syringe five times.
Boil the cell lysates in 1X LDS Sample buffer for 5 min.
Load the cell lysates on 4%–20% SurePAGE Bis-Tris precast gels.
Transfer resolved cell lysates onto nitrocellulose membrane.
Perform Western blot using anti-GFP antibody conjugated to HRP.
Seed 1 × 10^7 BS-C-1 cells in complete MEM-10 medium in T175 flask.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Dilute 500 μL of recombinant virus with 4.5 mL MEM-2.5.
Add diluted virus to infected cells and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Add 25 mL of MEM-2.5 to each flask and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 48 h.
Scrape cells with disposable cell scraper and transfer the culture supernatant to 50 mL conical tube.
Spin down the cells at 1800 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cell pellet in 2 mL MEM-2.5.
Subject the infected cell mixture to three cycles of freeze/thaw, vortexing after each thaw cycle.
Aliquot the viral supernatant into 2 mL screw cap freezing vials.
Store the viral supernatant at -80°C freezer.
Seed 5 × 10^5 Vero cells per well in 2 mL complete MEM-10 medium in a 6-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Thaw the virus from step 60 on ice.
Add 10 μL of stock virus solution to 990 μL of MEM-2.5.
Mix by gently pipetting the content several times.
Transfer 20 μL of the diluted virus with 180 μL of MEM-2.5.
Mix by gently pipetting the content several times.
Prepare the 10−4, 10−5, 10−6 and 10−7 dilutions as in previous steps.
Aspirate the culture medium in the 6-well plate.
Replace with 1 mL MEM-2.5 for each well.
Add 100 μL of the serially diluted virus to each well, leaving the last well as control without virus.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2 h.
Remove the medium.
Add 2 mL complete MEM to each well.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 48 h.
Wash cells twice with 2 mL 1X PBS.
Add 1 mL 4% paraformaldehyde solution in PBS.
Fix the cells for 30 min at 22°C.
Aspirate the paraformaldehyde solution.
Add 1 mL of crystal violet staining solution to each well.
Rock the plate gently to ensure that the solution covers the whole well.
Aspirate the crystal violet solution.
Rinse the wells under a running tap to remove the crystal violet solution.
Count the number of plaques in the wells with clear and distinct plaques.
Calculate the plaque forming unit (PFU) using the formula: PFU = Number of plaques x dilution factor x volume (ml).
Seed 1.25 x 10^5 L929 cells in 1 mL complete DMEM medium per well in a 24-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Thaw recombinant vaccinia virus rVACV-GFP-vIRD on ice.
Calculate the volume of stock virus needed using the formula: Volume of stock virus needed (ml) = MOI x cell number / PFU of stock (ml).
Replace the culture medium with DMEM-2.5 containing the calculated volume of rVACV-GFP-vIRD.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2 h.
Remove the medium containing the virus.
Replace it with 500 μL complete DMEM containing 100 nM Incucyte® Cytotox Red Dye.
Scan the plate using the Incucyte live cell imaging system every hour for up to 24 hours.
Analyze the results using Incucyte software version 2020B.
Calculate cell death by dividing the red fluorescent area (dying cells) over the green fluorescent area (infected cells).
If non-fluorescent viruses are used, calculate cell death using the phase area instead of the green fluorescent area.
Alternatively, calculate cell death using the number of fluorescent objects.
